parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**TGR Electronics**

TGR Electronics is a medium-sized manufacturer of smart home devices based in Country X. The company has been operating for 15 years and has grown steadily, now employing 250 people. TGR's main products include smart thermostats, security cameras, and voice-controlled lighting systems. The company uses a combination of automated production lines and skilled technicians to manufacture its products.

TGR's annual revenue last year was £50 million, with a profit of £5 million. The company currently sells its products primarily in Country X through a network of electronics retailers and its own website. However, TGR is now considering expanding into international markets, particularly in neighbouring countries.

The smart home device market is becoming increasingly competitive, with new entrants and rapidly changing technology. TGR's management team is debating whether to invest heavily in research and development (R&D) to create innovative new products or to focus on reducing costs to compete on price.

TGR is also facing challenges related to its supply chain. The company imports many of its components from overseas, and recent fluctuations in exchange rates have increased costs. Additionally, there is growing consumer concern about the environmental impact of electronic devices.

The company's Human Resources department is considering implementing a new training programme to upskill its workforce, particularly in the areas of software development and data analysis. However, this would require a significant investment.

TGR's management must make decisions about international expansion, product development strategy, and workforce training while navigating external challenges such as increased competition, supply chain issues, and environmental concerns.

Consider the impact of the following three stakeholder groups on TGR Electronics' decision-making:

- Shareholders
- Employees
- Customers

Which stakeholder group is likely to have the most influence on TGR's future strategy? **Justify **your choice.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/tgr-electronics-case-study.pdf) when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Shareholders want TGR to make more money. TGR made £5 million profit last year **[Ap]**. Shareholders might push for international expansion to increase profits further to maximise dividends and increase the share price **[An]**.

Employees are crucial for TGR's success. The company has 250 workers, including skilled technicians **[Ap]**. Employees would likely support the plan to upskill the workforce in software development and data analysis **[Ap]** as it could lead to better job security and higher wages. This may make them more committed to the firm **[An]**

Customers are vital for TGR's sales. Customers are worried about the environmental impact of electronic devices **[Ap]**, so TGR might need to develop more eco-friendly products to keep customers happy and maintain sales **[An]**

I think customers will have the most influence on TGR's future strategy **[E]**. The smart home device market is getting more competitive **[Ap]**, so keeping customers happy is crucial for TGR's success. Customers' growing concerns about the environmental impact of electronic devices **[Ap]** could shape what products TGR develops in the future. Most importantly, without satisfied customers buying their products, TGR will neither be able to make money for shareholders nor provide security or higher pay for their 250 skilled employees **[Ap]** so, by focusing on meeting customer needs, TGR can stay competitive and grow in the long term. This will benefit shareholders and employees too **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Shareholders**
> 
>   - Expect strong returns and dividends from £5 million profit → pressure to prioritise cost reduction over risky spending
>   - Support international expansion to grow the £50 million revenue base → back strategies that promise scale and market diversification
>   - Weigh R&D investment against short-term profitability → influence budget allocation between innovation and cost control
>   - Concerned about supply-chain risks (exchange-rate fluctuations) → push for local sourcing or hedging to protect margins
> - **Employees**
> 
>   - Skilled technicians and automated-line workers drive product quality and efficiency → influence whether to invest in upskilling or further automation
>   - HR’s training proposal in software and data analysis reflects workforce desire for development → may tip decisions in favour of R&D growth
>   - Fear of job losses from cost cuts → pressure to maintain existing operations and headcount over closures
>   - Employee buy-in essential for any environmental or process changes → affects rollout of sustainable manufacturing practices
> - **Customers**
> 
>   - Demand for cutting-edge smart home devices → compels heavy R&D investment to stay competitive in a fast-evolving market
>   - Price sensitivity in consumer segments → requires balancing innovation costs with affordable pricing strategies
>   - Growing environmental awareness → drives need for sustainable product design and transparent supply chains
>   - Shift toward e-commerce (22 % of sales) → shapes decisions on digital investment and channel focus
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Customers will exert the greatest influence on TGR’s future strategy because their evolving demands for innovation, value and sustainability directly determine sales and market positioning
>   - While shareholders set financial boundaries and employees enable execution, without meeting customer needs any strategy fails to drive revenue and profit
>   - TGR should prioritise market-led R&D and cost initiatives grounded in customer insights to satisfy consumers and deliver on shareholder expectations

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**RMT Clothing Ltd**

RMT Clothing Ltd is a medium-sized clothing retailer based in Country X. It was founded in 1995 and has grown to 50 stores across the country, selling affordable fashion for men and women aged 18-35. RMT currently employs 800 people, and had annual revenue of \$85 million last year.

The company is facing increasing competition from online retailers. RMT's CEO, Sarah Jones, is considering whether to close 10 underperforming stores and invest in expanding the company's e-commerce operations instead. This would involve making 100 store staff redundant but hiring 50 new employees to work on the website and in the distribution centre.

RMT's financial performance over the last 3 years is shown in table 1 below.

**Table 1: RMT’s Financial Performance 2020 to 2022**

| Year | Revenue (\$m) | Profit (\$m) | Online sales (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2020 | 80 | 4.0 | 15 |
| 2021 | 82 | 3.8 | 18 |
| 2022 | 85 | 3.5 | 22 |

The company's main stakeholders have differing views on the proposed changes. Shareholders are concerned about falling profits and want to see a clear plan for growth. Employees are worried about potential job losses. Customers have been complaining that RMT's website is difficult to use compared to competitors.

RMT is also facing external challenges including rising energy and material costs, as well as changing consumer preferences towards more sustainable fashion. However, there are opportunities to expand into new international markets through e-commerce.

Sarah needs to decide on the best strategy to ensure RMT's long-term success in a rapidly changing retail environment.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following two options for RMT to achieve its objective of improving financial performance:

- Close 10 stores and expand e-commerce operations
- Keep all stores open but reduce costs

Which option do you recommend? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/rmt-clothing-ltd-case-study.pdf) when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Online sales have been growing, reaching 22% in 2022 **[Ap]**, so RMT's customers are increasingly shopping online. Expanding e-commerce could help RMT compete better with online rivals, increasing market share **[An]**. It would also reduce costs from running physical stores, like rent and utilities, which could contribute to improving RMT's profit **[An]**. However, it would mean making 100 store staff redundant **[Ap]**, which could damage employee morale and RMT's reputation **[An]**

Keeping all stores open but reducing costs avoids job losses, which would please employees **[An]**. It maintains RMT's physical presence, which some customers prefer **[Ap]**. Costs could be reduced by negotiating better deals with suppliers, reducing inventory or cutting marketing expenses **[An]**. However, it might not improve profits enough, as RMT's profit has been declining despite increasing revenue **[An]** from \$80m to \$85m between 2020-2022 **[Ap]**

I recommend closing 10 stores and expanding e-commerce **[E]**. This recognises changing customer behaviour, with more and more buying RMT's products online **[Ap]**. While 100 jobs would be lost, 50 new jobs would be created in e-commerce and distribution **[Ap]** and there is potential to enter overseas markets by selling online **[E]**. While shareholder concerns about falling profits would be addressed by reducing costs, simply cutting costs and carrying on operating stores doesn't address the fundamental market changes and limits potential to gain new customers, especially in other countries **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Close 10 stores and expand e-commerce operations**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Reduces fixed costs by closing 10 underperforming stores → cuts rent and staffing expenses
>     - Frees up funds to improve the online platform and distribution centre → meets customer demand for easier web shopping
>     - Online sales have risen from 15 % in 2020 to 22 % in 2022 → aligns investment with a growing channel
>     - Focuses the store network on profitable locations → increases average revenue per remaining store
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - 100 store-staff redundancies vs only 50 new online roles → net loss of jobs may harm staff morale and public image
>     - Loss of physical presence in 10 communities → risks alienating loyal local shoppers
>     - Upfront investment needed for website upgrades and warehouse expansion → may strain cash flow in the short term
>     - Reduced ability for customers to try on products in-store → could weaken omnichannel experience
> - **Keep all stores open but reduce costs**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Protects all 800 employees’ jobs → maintains morale and local goodwill
>     - Retains full network of 50 stores → preserves brand visibility and customer convenience
>     - Cost cuts (e.g. negotiate rent reductions, streamline staffing rotas, bulk-buy supplies) → improves margins without closing sites
>     - Less disruptive for customers and staff → avoids the risks of large-scale closures
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Cost savings may be too small to reverse falling profits → limited impact on overall financial performance
>     - Risk of cutting too deeply → service levels or product quality could suffer, driving customers away
>     - Underperforming stores continue to lose money → ongoing drain on resources that could fund growth
>     - Delay in e-commerce investment → competitors may pull further ahead online
> - **Recommendation**
> 
>   - Close 10 stores and expand e-commerce is the stronger choice to improve financial performance because it delivers larger, more immediate cost savings and aligns with clear growth in online sales
>   - To balance the impact on staff and customers, RMT should offer generous redundancy packages, retrain some store staff for online roles, and maintain an omnichannel focus by enhancing click-and-collect services
>   - This strategy uses savings from store closures to fund a robust e-commerce upgrade, positioning RMT for long-term success in a digital retail environment

**Everyone Theatre (ET) **

Zane and Zaara are both actors. They plan to start up a theatre in a low-income area of Main City. Zane and Zaara believe that helping the community is as important as being successful entrepreneurs.

The theatre will be a private sector business and Zane and Zaara have to decide whether to start up as an unincorporated business (partnership) or as a limited company. Zane is planning to prepare a cash-flow forecast for the first year. Zaara knows they will need to set business objectives for the theatre and also decide on a leadership style to use when managing employees. ET will have 24 part-time employees as shown in the organisational chart in Appendix 1.

Zane and Zaara plan to put on performances in the evenings for local people and tourists. There will be 100 seats in the theatre but not all the seats will be sold if the price is too high. The Marketing Manager, Zaara, will need to decide which performances to put on, what price to charge and which refreshments to sell. Zaara will also need to decide between the two possible options for the first performance when the theatre opens. Information on the two options is shown in Appendix 2.

In the daytime the theatre building will be used by Daycare, a local social enterprise. Daycare takes care of young children up to the age of 5 so that low-income family members can go out to work. It also provides education for the children which helps their development and progress before they start school. Some of Daycare’s objectives are different to those of ET

**Appendix 1 **

**Proposed organisational chart for the theatre**

Note: The numbers in brackets are the number of part-time employees who work in each department

**Appendix 2 **

**Forecast data for the two possible options for ET’s first performance at the theatre**

| For each performance | **Option 1** | **Option 2** |
|---|---|---|
| Number of actors/employees | 7 | 24 |
| Average wage cost per actor/employee | \$30 | \$10 |
| All other costs including scenery, costumes and promotion | \$1000 | \$2000 |
| Forecast revenue assuming all 100 seats are sold | \$1000 | \$2500 |

**Appendix 3 **

**Email from Zane to Zaara**

**To: Zaara **

**From: Zane **

**Date: 1 April 2023**

We want to support the local community and we need to make decisions about the following.

Should we:

- Pay fair wages even though they may be higher than those paid by competing theatres?
- Only buy costumes produced in the local community?
- Purchase all refreshments from suppliers that do not pollute the environment?

**Explain one **business objective for ET and one other objective that a social enterprise like Daycare might have.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
One business objective for ET could be survival **[K]** in their first year of operation. As a new business, ET will need to make sure it covers its costs to avoid going bankrupt **[An]**. This is especially important when opening in a low-income area of Main City **[Ap]**, which may make it challenging to sell enough tickets. Survival would allow ET to continue putting on performances to serve the local community **[An]**

A different objective that Daycare, as a social enterprise, might have is to provide a service to the community **[K]**. Daycare takes care of young children up to age 5 from low-income families during the day **[Ap],** which allows parents and guardians to go to work. This helps to increase their family's income, improve their living standards **[An],** and support their children's development before starting school. This focuses on creating social value rather than just making a profit **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two full paragraphs, one for each reason/point
> - In each paragraph:
> 
>   - State one valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain how it works using a cause–effect chain → up to 2 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant answers might include:
> 
>   - Business objective for ET
>   - Survival – to not go bankrupt in the first year of operation – to cover costs
>   - Profit – to provide a return on investment – for the owners who risked their own money
>   - Growth of the business – to possibly increase sales – leading to increased revenue in the future
>   - Market share – attract a higher number of customers – possibly leading to higher revenue
> - Other objectives for social enterprise
> 
>   - Service to the community/help local people – to create jobs for people in the local area – support  is advantaged groups in society/make a profit to put back into local initiatives
>   - Provide childcare to enable low-income parents/carers to go out to work – increase their incomes – raising their living standards
>   - Provide education for the pre-school children of low-income families
>   - Provides access to education that otherwise would not be provided
>   - Improves the likelihood of these children being more successful when they do go to school/may improve their ability to earn higher incomes in the future/get a better paid job
>   - To provide funds to reinvest back into the social enterprise – by making a profit
>   - To break-even
> - Application might include: pre-school children; theatre; performances; actors; pay fair wages; tourists; low-income area; 24 part-time employees; provides education for children under 5

**Safari Adventures (SA) **

Tokumbo is a sole trader. He started SA 2 years ago in country X. Tokumbo had previously worked for a company selling holidays. SA organises safari tours which take tourists to view wild animals on a game reserve. Most of SA’s customers are tourists from other countries. Tokumbo did not have any objectives when he started SA but knows they are important for his business.

SA uses its own vehicles for the 7 day safari tours and provides accommodation in small local hotels. Tokumbo employs 4 safari guides, 1 for each of the 4 vehicles. The safari guides drive the tourists around the game reserve. There is 1 additional employee who helps Tokumbo in the office with administration. Tokumbo thinks SA needs a website so tourists can book directly with them rather than booking through holiday companies that charge SA a fee.

Tokumbo is considering the following three options for the future growth of SA safari tours:

- Option 1 - increasing the number of safari guides and vehicles to increase the number of customers from the existing target market
- Option 2 – targeting young people who want to camp and sleep in a tent on their safari
- Option 3 - targeting high-income tourists who prefer to stay in luxury hotels

Information about these three options is outlined in Appendix 3.

Tokumbo plans to provide more training for his employees whichever option he chooses. He wants his existing employees to have a wider knowledge of the wild animals on the game reserve and to be able to provide high-quality customer service. Tokumbo has to decide which method of training to use.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News, September 2022 **

**Tourism takes off**

Country X is becoming a popular holiday destination for tourists from other countries.

There is an increased demand from high-income tourists who want to stay in luxury hotels whilst on safari tours. These tourists are willing to pay high prices. There is also a new trend for younger people who want cheaper holidays. They prefer to camp and sleep in tents on game reserves rather than stay in hotels.

Are the many safari businesses in country X ready to target these new markets?

The use of e-commerce to find and book safari tours by tourists from other countries is offering both opportunities and threats to businesses in country X.

The inflation rate in country X has increased to 4% which may affect some of our local safari businesses.

**Appendix 2 **

**Email from Tokumbo’s accountant**

To: Tokumbo

From: Accountant

Subject: Source of finance for the new vehicles

New vehicles will be needed whichever option you choose for the future growth of your business.

I have considered several sources of finance you could use for the new vehicles. Interest rates on bank loans have fallen to 2% whilst interest rates on savings are 3%. I think you should choose from one of the following sources:

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

We can meet to discuss these sources if that would help you to decide.

**Appendix 3 **

**SA’s three options for a 7 day safari tour**

|   | Option 1 More existing safari tours | Option 2 Camping safari tours | Option 3 Luxury safari tours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forecast number of tourists per week | 16 | 32 | 10 |
| Total costs per week for SA to provide these safari tours | \$12 000 | \$8000 | \$20 000 |
| Average cost per tourist | \$750 | ? | ? |
| Price per tourist | \$1000 | \$400 | \$2400 |

**Explain four** business objectives Tokumbo could set for SA.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2022-paper-21-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Tokumbo could set an objective to increase profit **[K]** to give him funds to pay for the new website he's thinking about **[Ap]**

He could set an objective to grow the business **[K]** by adding more safari guides and vehicles** [Ap]**

Improving customer service **[K] **by training employees about wild animals and customer care **[Ap]**

He could set the objective to increase market share **[K]** from the growing tourism industry in country X **[Ap]**

> **[case-study]**
> BKH is a large public limited company. It has 2 000 employees across 18 locations. BKH sells a range of insurance products, including house and car insurance. BKH’s shareholders want the business to increase profit. The Managing Director knows  increasing profit can conflict with the objectives of other stakeholder groups. She said: ‘Private sector businesses have different objectives to public sector organisations.’ BKH is also planning to expand by taking over another insurance company.

**Explain one** way each stakeholder’s objectives might conflict with BKH’s objective to increase profit.

Customers want lower prices **[K]** for their house and car insurance **[Ap]**, which conflicts with BKH's profit goal. If BKH keeps prices lower, this reduces profit per policy. Cheaper car insurance policies may attract more customers, but less will be earned on each policy sold **[An]**

BKH's 2,000 employees across 18 locations **[Ap]** desire higher wages **[K]**. Paying higher salaries increases costs and lowers profit. If BKH raises wages by 5% for all 2000 employees, this would significantly increase expenses and reduce profit margins **[An]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> You should not include shareholders in your analysis, as they are the stakeholder group keen to increase profit

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two developed paragraphs, one for each part of the question
> - For each paragraph:
> 
>   - State a valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the business in the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain the impact using a cause–effect chain → 1 An mark
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Customers
>

>     - Desire high-quality customer service [k] which requires more than 2000 staff [app] increasing costs/expenses [an]
>     - May want offices in more locations [k] than 18 [app] which could increase costs [an]
>   - Employees
>

>     - May require job security / contract [k] after the takeover [app]
>     - Job satisfaction / motivation / training / promotion [k]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

parts.problem_md: Do you think the shareholders are the most important stakeholder group to the success of a limited company? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Shareholders provide finance to help a business expand and buy equipment **[K]**, which can increase output and ensure it meets customer demand. They can influence the company's aims **[K]**, often focusing on maximising profits over other objectives, meaning that customer needs are less central to business activities **[An]**

Other stakeholders like customers are vital too as they buy the products **[K]**. Without enough customers, revenue will not cover costs and the business would struggle to survive **[An]**

Shareholders are important as they invest money in the company, which can help it expand. However, once the company is established, they have little influence over day-to-day decisions **[E]** unless they are directors or managers. Customers always matter, as they buy the products, which determines ongoing success, so customer are probably the most important stakeholders** [E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Shareholders/owners
>   
>     - Provide finance / invest money / capital in business [k] which can help the business expand / buy more equipment [an] so can increase output [an]
>     - Influence the aims of the business [k]
>     - Have the power to vote out the directors [k]
>     - They have little / no influence over day-to-day decisions [k]

>

>     - Customers [k] matter as they buy the products [an]. While shareholders provide important finance, without customers even a limited company cannot generate income [eval] and without this cannot cover its costs or make a profit, so the customer is probably the most important stakeholder. parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Gemma’s Jewels (GJ)**

Gemma set up GJ as a sole trader 5 years ago in country Z. She started by selling rings and bracelets from a rented shop. She used her own savings to start the business. The first year was successful. After this first year Gemma decided to expand by selling more expensive items of jewellery. Gemma thinks it is important to set clear business objectives. She wants her business to increase sales by 10% each year and to increase market share.

As the business grew Gemma needed more finance for a computer, inventory and working capital to avoid liquidity problems. She decided to convert the business to a private limited company and sell shares to members of her family. Gemma still owns more than 50% of the shares in GJ.

In 2019, Gemma purchased a franchise from Beautywise Jewellery. This means GJ is now only able to sell Beautywise products in its shop. GJ has to purchase all of its inventory from Beautywise and in addition pay 20% of gross profit to Beautywise. More details about the franchise are in the advertisement in Appendix 1.

Gemma has developed a website so customers can order online. Customers can also download a mobile (cell) phone app to view and order jewellery.

Gemma plans to open a second shop as a Beautywise franchise in a nearby town. She has to decide which method of sales promotion to use. GJ needs to recruit a manager for the new shop. The manager will be responsible for operating the shop and making most of the decisions about which items of inventory to buy. The manager will also need to ensure excellent customer service is provided and that the new employees are motivated and working efficiently.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for Beautywise Jewellery Franchise**

**Become a franchisee to sell Beautywise Jewellery and improve your chances of success!!**

What we offer you:

- Be the only shop in your area that sells Beautywise jewellery
- Beautywise will advertise nationally on television and in newspapers
- Help and advice on decoration of the shop and training for employees and the franchisee
- Ethically sourced jewellery imported especially for Beautywise
- The franchise fee is just \$50 000 per year!

**Appendix 2 **

**Newspaper article- Daily News **

**External factors affecting the jewellery market in country Z**

The demand for jewellery in country Z is likely to be affected by some recent changes. Consumers are becoming more aware of the ethical issues involved in jewellery production in some countries. The exchange rate of the currency of country Z is likely to depreciate over the next 12 months. The Government is planning changes to tax rates which might reduce the effects of the current economic boom.

**Appendix 3 **

**Information on three possible locations for the new shop**

| **Annual costs** | **Town A** | **Town B** | **Town C** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shop rent | \$45 000 per year for 5 years | \$35 000 per year for 10 years | \$20 000 per year for 15 years |
| Wages and salaries | \$80 000 | \$70 000 | \$60 000 |
| Heating and lighting | \$5 000 | \$5 000 | \$3 000 |
| Estimated gross profit | \$400 000 | \$300 000 | \$200 000 |

Note: Franchise fee is \$50 000 per year and 20% of gross profit is paid to Beautywise.

**Explain two **reasons why having business objectives is important to Gemma.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Objectives give Gemma a clear target to work towards **[K]**. These specific goals guide Gemma's decisions and actions, keeping her focused on business growth **[An]**. These objectives might influence her decision to open a second Beautywise franchise shop **[Ap] **and determine whether it would be the best way to achieve the overall business aim **[An]**

Objectives allow Gemma to measure the success of her business **[K]**. By setting targets like a 10% annual sales increase **[Ap]**, Gemma can track her progress over time by comparing actual sales figures to her goal **[An]**. This helps Gemma know if her strategies are working or if she needs to make changes to improve performance and achieve her growth aims **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two full paragraphs, one for each reason/point
> - In each paragraph:
> 
>   - State one valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain how it works using a cause–effect chain → up to 2 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant reasons might include:
> 
>   - A clear target/aim/purpose for owner to work towards – guides the business in the right direction - avoids loss of focus
>   - Decision-making will be focused on the objectives – meaning better decisions are taken – the business would be more efficient
>   - Clear objectives will help focus the employees and management on the same goal – helps motivate employees - making it more likely to be achieved
>   - Allows measurement of success – can judge performance or progress
>   - Comparison of performance - so business managers at each shop can compare how the shop has performed against their objective(s) - to see whether or not it has been successful
>   - Award a maximum of 3 additional marks for each explanation – one of which must be applied to this context.
> - Application could include:
> 
>   - Increase market share
>   - Increase sales by 10% each year
>   - Jewellery, rings and bracelets
>   - She plans to open a second shop
